text:
olivia: Heads-up — saw some flip-flopping in route arbitration for tenant-42 when region_preference + cost_cap are both present. Requests bounce between EU and US backends for identical traffic patterns. :thinking:

sam: ugh, saw that too earlier. looks like tie-breaker is non-deterministic when score delta < 0.02. logs show alternating penalty updates.

cheng: can you paste a trace? small repro would help. is this only with hedged requests or normal single-shot?

olivia: single-shot. attaching trimmed trace below (timestamps redacted):
```
route_eval: candidate A score 0.712
route_eval: candidate B score 0.705
penalty_update: candidate B penalty decayed -> 0.002
selected: B
next_request: candidate A score 0.713
selected: A
```

maria: that pattern screams low-resolution weights + immediate cache invalidation. our current tie-breaker is random when within epsilon. we should prefer stability unless cost delta is meaningful. :thumbsup:

dan: agree — add hysteresis so we don't flip on <500ms worth of observed latency variance. also, add a deterministic tie-breaker ordered by (tenant affinity, region affinity, id).

sam: proposed quick config to try in staging: 
```
matcher: region_and_cost
weights:
  latency: 0.55
  cost: 0.35
  region_affinity: 0.1
tie_break_threshold: 0.03
hysteresis_ms: 500
tie_break_policy: deterministic_stable
cache_ttl_ms: 300000
```

cheng: two questions: 1) how does this interact with KV cache invalidation? we recently set prefix-cache TTL to 1s in the hot path. 2) if we increase cache_ttl_ms we may harm burst elasticity.

maria: for (1) we should separate scoring cache vs KV prefix cache. scoring cache can be conservative (300s) for stability; KV prefix cache stays short. for (2) fine to have tiered TTLs per traffic class. low-latency interactive gets lower TTL. batch workloads can have longer TTLs.

olivia: +1 on tiered TTL. tenant-42 is interactive so keep KV short, but scoring TTL can be longer. can we add a decay on penalty so long-lived cheap candidates don't starve?

dan: decaying penalty is already possible — set penalty_half_life_ms. but we should cap decay so it doesn't immediately reselect a cold GPU that will thrash warmups. maybe combine with warmup_cost_estimate.

sam: here's a small patch idea: deterministic tie-breaker picks candidate with smallest stable_penalty -> then region_affinity -> then lower cost. fallback to id. will run sim overnight.

infra-bot: deploy queued: routing-service-staging v3.14.2 -> canary (started)

maria: while sim runs, add a metric: "route_flip_rate" per tenant, and an alert if > 0.5% over 5m. also log tie_break_reason on selects.

cheng: re: observability — add a histogram of score_deltas at select time. that'll show how often we hit the epsilon band.

olivia: filed a follow-up issue: https://redwood.internal/issue/RI-8812 — summary + perf dumps. tagging @sam @maria.

sam: thanks — if sim looks good i'll push the tie-breaker change to canary tonight.

dan: small gotcha: make sure rollout respects Dedicated vs Hosted defaults — Dedicated tenants might want stronger region_affinity. maybe allowable override in tenant config.

maria: yup. include tenant_override: prefer_region: true in the policy envelope.

olivia: cool. next steps: 1) sim run 2) add metrics/alerts 3) canary tie-breaker 4) RFC short doc for hysteresis and scoring cache TTL. i'll draft RFC tomorrow. :memo:

sam: sounds good. if anyone sees weird regressions ping #eng-runtime and @oncall.

infra-bot: canary deployment succeeded: routing-service-staging v3.14.2 -> 3/3 canaries healthy

olivia: thanks team. closing thread for now, will update RI-8812 with results later. :rocket:
